en.h: A recreation area in northern Idaho, almost entirely in Benewah County. Founded in 1908, it is the oldest state or provincial park in the Pacific Northwest. It has 5,744 acres (2,325 ha) of land and 2,332 acres (944 ha) of water on three lakes, Benewah, Chatcolet and Hidden, linked to Lake Coeur d'Alene since a 1906 dam raised the water. The Coeur d'Alene people were its first inhabitants. Camping, boating, hiking, riding and fishing go on year-round.
